rationale: Start with a broad gradient to locate the elution window and critical pairs while minimizing the risk of missing strongly retained compounds. A moderate temperature leaves room to probe temperature-dependent selectivity in either direction.

Lengthen only the gradient to test whether the critical pair responds to reduced steepness. The current 8.30-minute last peak leaves room to improve resolution while likely keeping all peaks within 10 minutes.

The critical pair improves with a shallower gradient but remains below target. Raise temperature alone to test its selectivity response and shorten retention, potentially creating room for further slope reduction.

The central peak pattern suggests the critical pair crossed between 40 and 50 C, so further heating may separate it again. Return to the steeper 12-minute gradient to favor separation on this side of the crossing and keep the last peak comfortably below 10 minutes.
Injection 4 reaches the maximum CRF; retain it as the benchmark. Shorten the gradient by one grid step to test for a faster fully resolved method, watching both marginal pairs.

Shift the gradient window upward while preserving injection 4’s successful slope of 0.075 organic fraction per minute. This tests whether a stronger start can shorten retention without sacrificing either critical pair; the final organic fraction remains well above the observed elution window.

Test a faster, hotter selectivity regime while retaining injection 4 as the maximum-score benchmark. Heating and steepening may carry the newly limiting pair through an elution-order reversal and separate it on the other side.

Test whether a substantially steeper gradient resolves the limiting pair after its apparent order reversal at 60 C. This explores a much faster regime, while checking for new co-elutions among the other central peaks and retaining injection 4 as the benchmark.

Return to the near-successful injection 6 and reduce its gradient slope slightly by lowering phi1. This should improve the limiting pair while potentially retaining full resolution in less time than injection 4.

Explore the cooler selectivity regime with a short gradient, since the hotter regime develops competing critical pairs when compressed. Lower temperature may separate the central cluster in a different order; injection 4 remains the maximum-score fallback.

Test a stronger starting solvent at 60 C to seek a faster separation on the reversed-order side of the limiting pair. Monitor the first peaks for loss of retention and the central cluster for new overlaps; injection 4 remains the maximum-CRF benchmark.

A stronger start may further separate the reversed critical pair, while a slightly shallower slope should help protect its neighboring pair. Check early-peak resolution carefully because the first compound is approaching the unretained region.

Return to injection 9 and lower phi1 one grid step to extend its observed improvement in the limiting pair toward R ≥ 1.5. This tests a second fully resolved method with a shorter programmed gradient, while retaining injection 4 as the fastest confirmed maximum-score benchmark.

Test cooling relative to injection 2 to separate its critical pair on the opposite side of the temperature-dependent crossing. The last peak should remain near but below 10 minutes; monitor the neighboring central pairs for competing losses in resolution.
